source_text: Affligetis animas vestras; sabbatum sabbatorum. Ieiunium a vitiis. Dies propitiationis.
thought_title: Fasting from vices on the day of propitiation
orientation: Origen is explaining the spiritual meaning of the Day of Atonement commands from Leviticus, applying them to the Christian soul's fasting from sin.
pass_a_gloss: You shall afflict your souls; a sabbath of sabbaths. A fast from vices. The day of propitiation.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the future indicative command, preserving the second-person plural and the direct object 'souls' as the seat of self-denial.
Literal rendering of the Hebrew superlative construction, keeping the repetition that marks the day's supreme solemnity.
Preserves the ablative of separation 'a vitiis' and the noun 'ieiunium' as Origen's spiritual gloss on afflicting the soul.
Literal rendering of the genitive construction, keeping the technical term 'propitiation' for the atonement day.

pass_b_english: "You shall afflict your souls; it is a sabbath of sabbaths" (Leviticus 16:31). A fast from vices. The day of propitiation.
